label: first token is q/e/x (t=0); plus the first copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Two parts. (1) At t=0 it fires whenever the first input token is q, e or x, and on every such step (dev precision 1.0, about 91% of active steps, 84% of activation mass). The value is fixed per token: q about 0.19 of max, x about 0.17, e about 0.04. It never fires at t=0 for any other token. (2) At step L+1 (recall_idx 1, where the input is the fed-back orig(0) and the output is orig(1)) it fires mostly when L=3, on about 37% of those steps, plus a few L=4 cases (70 steps). These carry the largest activations (up to max, e.g. n c f <DEL> [n] c), and the strength varies with the sequence content. The last original token (c/d/f/o/r/digits) raises the firing rate there to about 68%. It is silent at t=1..3, at the delimiter, and at all later copy steps, and the rest of the original phase does not depend on the token. On dev, the t=0 clause alone gets F1 0.95 / mass 0.84, and adding the L=3 copy clause gets F1 0.93 / mass 0.995.

issues: The t=0 part holds up. (t==0) & q/e/x has dev precision 1.0, recall 0.907 and mass 0.841. t=0 with any other token is never active (0 of 89,999 steps). The unit is also silent at t=1..3, at the delimiter and at copy steps beyond recall_idx 1.

The copy clause is the main systematic source of false positives. (recall_idx==1)&(L==3) has precision of only 0.365 (dev). On test, 1,719 of 1,802 predicate-true-but-inactive steps are L=3 first-copy steps. The label says 'plus the first copy step of length-3 sequences', which reads as unconditional. In fact it fires on only about a third of those steps.

Whether the unit fires at the L=3 first copy step depends on all three original tokens, not mainly on the last one. Precision by token ranges from 0.0 (orig(0)=r) to 0.89 (orig(0)=q) for orig(0), from 0.05 to 0.71 for orig(1), and from 0.08 to 0.73 for orig(2). The explanation focuses on the last token being c/d/f/o/r/digits, which leaves out most of this dependence.
The claim that a last token of c/d/f/o/r/digits raises the firing rate to about 68% did not check out: it measures 0.60 on dev.
The L=4 part is negligible (70 steps, precision 0.005), and the predicate correctly leaves it out. The remaining misses (87 on test) are scattered L=4 first-copy steps and hold 0.6% of the mass.
